newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: DIEGO MARADONA'S MANAGER CHARGED WITH SELLING DRUGS.
newsitem.headline: DIEGO MARADONA'S MANAGER CHARGED WITH SELLING DRUGS.

text.p: The manager of Argentine soccer idol Diego Maradona, Guillermo Coppola, was charged on Thursday with possessing drugs for sale and remanded into custody.
But Judge Hernan Bernasconi did not press charges for drug-trafficking, the state-run Telam news agency reported.

Three other men were also charged in the case, but no charges were pressed against former Argentine national team soccer player Alberto Tarantini. Tarantini, however, was ordered to stay in a rehabilitation centre until he overcomes drug addiction.
The judge also ordered that goods up to $100,000 in value belonging to each of the four accused be embargoed. They face jail sentences of between six to 20 years if convicted.

A prominent member of Argentina's glitzy jet-set and a gossip page companion of models and politicians, the tanned, white-haired Coppola turned himself in to police this month after almost a day on the run following a pre-dawn drugs raid on his luxury Buenos Aires apartment. Police found about two pounds (one kg) of cocaine buried in a flower vase.

Coppola had reportedly been monitored by police for months and his phone was tapped. He said the drugs found were not his and testified that he had left Maradona alone with women at the apartment days before the bust.

The case has attracted enormous media attention in Argentina and the sight of Coppola being hustled through a frenzied media pack by burly policemen in and out of judge's offices has claimed a regular spot on television newscasts.
A distraught Maradona, once the most expensive player in the world and the star of Argentina's 1986 World Cup triumph, this week blamed his close friend's arrest on unidentified political interests.
Maradona, a confessed cocaine addict who has had brushes with the law himself, was due to be called to testify as a witness in the Coppola case.
